principle: The Secondary Story owns the universal chapters-three-and-four sequence plus its following Before You Leave note block. Atlas editorial work chooses two distinct activity-specific chapter angles and one final editorial note from verified information. No slot is inherently about time, conditions or any other fixed topic.

presentation.layout: one Field Card photo on the left and two editorial chapters stacked on the right
presentation.pageStyle: new light Field Card sheet on the shared paper background

beforeYouLeave.layout: one editorial text on the left and one fixed-position post-it on the right

chapters.selectionRule: Choose the two strongest distinct next angles not already explained by the Primary Story chapters. They may cover timing, conditions, etiquette, equipment, seasonality, context or any other verified subject that materially improves the visit.
chapters.antiPattern: Do not force chapter 03 to be TIME or chapter 04 to be CONDITIONS. Do not repeat the Primary Story angles merely to fill the layout.

body.selectionRule: Use one final editorial angle that adds perspective or a last useful way to approach the activity without becoming a second chapter pair.

note.selectionRule: Use one concise practical field note that complements rather than summarizes the Before You Leave text.

shape.chapters: exactly two { label, title, body } objects
shape.beforeYouLeave: one { title, body, note: { label, text } } object

generationInput.subsequentSections: When fieldCardSecondaryStory is supplied, candidate.sections contains only later Field Card chapters after chapter 04.
